rv.q: This might be a work of outlandish genius, or a devised end of year A-level project featuring world-class actors (led by Ralph Fiennes and Francesca Annis).

Through glitchy video calls, he connects with his twin brother Richard, housebound, lost, and craving intimacy. Fiennes is compelling as Larry: a man hollowed by shame, eyes often lowered as if trying to avoid the truth.
Ralph Fiennes stars in Rebecca Lenkiewicz’s opaque new play
As the last of three productions presented under Ralph Fiennes’ stewardship in Bath, Small Hotel offers some of the best work of the season.

Intriguing yes, entertaining yes, but while this production deserves to be a sell-out due to the quality of the acting – and no doubt will be thanks to fans of Fiennes and Annis – you’re likely to leave feeling decidedly unrewarded by the play, which not only offers us themes of resentment and regret, but is a missed opportunity in itself.
Small Hotel is a triumph not because it provides easy answers, but because it doesn't try to.
